mission: Simplex believes that understanding intelligence is safety. It develops a rigorous theory of the internal structure of neural networks, drawing on computational mechanics, to explain how networks organise what they learn and how that relates to their behaviour, in both artificial and biological intelligence.

key_work.title: Transformers represent belief state geometry in their residual stream
key_work.plain_summary: Transformers trained to predict sequences build an internal geometric map of their beliefs about hidden states, exactly as the theory predicts.

key_work.title: Constrained belief updates explain geometric structures in transformer representations
key_work.plain_summary: Shows transformers implement a form of Bayesian belief updating shaped by their architecture.

key_work.title: Next-token pretraining implies in-context learning
key_work.plain_summary: Argues in-context learning arises predictably from ordinary next-token training.

key_work.title: Transformers learn factored representations
key_work.plain_summary: Transformers discover that the world splits into independent parts and store each part in its own subspace.

key_work.plain_summary: Overview of Simplex's research programme and results.

warnings.text: AI systems are deployed across society and we don't know how they work.
Without genuine understanding we can't reliably monitor, control, or reason about what these systems are doing.

recommendations.text: Build a real science of intelligence and of networks' internal structure as the foundation for safety.
Use AI systems as testbeds for theories of intelligence, artificial and biological.
